questions.question: What does it mean for a sequence $(a_n)_{n = 1}^{\infty}$ to converge to $L$?
options: Every term of the sequence equals $L$
Only the first term must be close to $L$.
questions.explanation: Convergence to $L$ means every positive accuracy request is eventually met by every remaining term, not merely by selected terms.
questions.source_support: The definition says that for every $\varepsilon \gt 0$ there is $N$ such that for all $n\ \ge N$, $|a_n-L| \lt \varepsilon$.
option_explanations: Terms may approach $L$ without ever equalling it, as $1/n\to0$.
The first term is irrelevant to long-run convergence.
Convergent sequences may oscillate, such as $(-1)^n/n\to0$.

questions.question: What is true about every convergent real sequence?
